seen_20q.question: How does Bucinca et al 2021 To Trust or to Think arXiv v1 address "Reduce Overreliance on AI in AI-assisted Decision-making"?
seen_20q.reference_answer: ZANA BUÇINCA, Harvard University, USA MAJA BARBARA MALAYA, Lodz University of Technology, Poland KRZYSZTOF Z. GAJOS, Harvard University, USA People supported by AI-powered decision support tools frequently overrely on the AI: they accept an AI’s suggestion even when that suggestion is wrong. Adding explanations to the AI decisions does not appear to reduce the overreliance and some studies suggest that it might even increase it.
seen_20q.answer: In this paper we argue that the current tendency of many researchers to rely heavily on pre-programmed machine learning models for decision making is one of the main reasons why people are over-relying on AI systems. We propose an alternative approach: to trust rather than think when using AI. In our view, it is important to be able to think critically about how AI works and what its limitations are before trusting it with decisions. Our proposal can be implemented by training humans to explain their use of AI systems (e.g., through natural language processing) and then using these explanations to guide future AI development.
